title: Resume review
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and an advisor at the career center.

lines.t: Hi, I was hoping to get my resume reviewed before the career fair on Thursday.
Sure. Unfortunately, all of our one-on-one slots are booked until next week. It's always like this before the fair.
Oh no. Is there anything else I can do?
Two options. We're running a drop-in resume workshop tomorrow at four. Or you can upload your resume online, and someone will send you comments within forty-eight hours.
Hmm, forty-eight hours would be cutting it close. I'll go to the workshop.
Good choice. Bring a printed copy, and you'll get feedback right there.

questions.prompt: Why does the woman go to the career center?
options: To sign up for the career fair
To get feedback on her resume
To find out about job openings
To print copies of her resume
optionNotes: She mentions the fair only as her deadline.
Printing is the advisor's later advice.
questions.explanation: She wants her resume reviewed before Thursday's career fair.
questions.evidence: I was hoping to get my resume reviewed before the career fair on Thursday.

questions.prompt: Why does the woman choose the workshop instead of the online option?
options: The online comments might not arrive in time.
She does not have a digital copy of her resume.
The workshop is free and the online service is not.
She prefers to meet the advisor one-on-one.
optionNotes: Correct: 'cutting it close' means there might not be enough time before Thursday.
questions.explanation: 'Cutting it close' means leaving very little time. Forty-eight hours might be too late for the Thursday fair.
questions.evidence: forty-eight hours would be cutting it close

title: Broken washing machines
context: Listen to a conversation between two students who live in the same dormitory.

lines.t: Did you manage to do your laundry? Two of the machines downstairs are broken again.
No, I gave up. Somebody put up a sign saying out of order, but it doesn't look like anyone's actually reported it.
I'll submit a maintenance request online. Last time, they fixed them in a day once someone finally filed one.
Thanks. In the meantime, I really need clean clothes for my interview on Friday.
There's a laundromat on Pine Street. It's a bit pricey, but it's open twenty-four hours.
That works. I'll go after dinner.

questions.prompt: What does the man offer to do?
options: Fix the machines himself
Lend the woman some clothes
Report the problem online
Drive the woman to the laundromat
optionNotes: Correct: he'll submit a maintenance request.
He only tells her where it is.
questions.explanation: He offers to file a maintenance request, since nobody has done it yet.
questions.evidence: I'll submit a maintenance request online.

questions.prompt: Why does the woman need clean clothes soon?
options: She has an interview on Friday.
She is going away for the weekend.
She has a sports game after dinner.
She is moving to another dormitory.
questions.explanation: She says she needs clean clothes for her Friday interview.
questions.evidence: I really need clean clothes for my interview on Friday.

title: Meal card declined
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a cafeteria worker.

lines.t: Hi, my meal card isn't working. It just beeped and said declined, and I've got class in ten minutes.
Let me see. Ah, it says your meal plan ran out yesterday. Did you buy the plan for the fall or for the whole year?
Just the fall, I think. I meant to renew it.
You can renew it online or at the housing office. For today, you can pay with cash or a credit card.
Okay, I'll pay by card now and renew it this afternoon.

questions.prompt: Why was the man's meal card declined?
options: The card was damaged.
His meal plan had ended.
He used the wrong card.
The machine was not working.
optionNotes: Correct: the plan ran out yesterday.
The machine worked; the plan had expired.
questions.explanation: The worker checks and finds that his plan ran out the day before.
questions.evidence: it says your meal plan ran out yesterday

options: Pay with cash and renew the plan online
Go to the housing office immediately
Pay by card now and renew the plan later
Eat somewhere else today
optionNotes: He'll renew it in the afternoon, not now.
questions.explanation: He says he'll pay by card and renew the plan in the afternoon.
questions.evidence: I'll pay by card now and renew it this afternoon.

title: After-hours lab access
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a lab manager.

lines.t: Hi, I'm working on my senior thesis, and I need to run experiments in the evenings. Is it possible to get after-hours access to the lab?
It's possible, but there's a catch. You'd need to complete the advanced safety training first, and the next session isn't until the twentieth.
The twentieth? My data's due to my advisor by the end of the month. That leaves me barely a week.
I understand. Actually, there's an online version of the training, but it's about six hours long, and most people find it pretty dull.
Dull I can handle. Losing two weeks I can't.
Fair enough. Once you pass the quiz at the end, send me the certificate, and I'll activate your card the same day.

questions.prompt: What is the woman's attitude toward the online training?
options: She is willing to do it even though it may be boring.
She thinks it will be too difficult.
She would prefer to attend the in-person session.
She doubts it will be accepted by the lab.
optionNotes: Correct: she accepts that it's dull because saving time matters more.
Difficulty isn't her concern; boredom is mentioned, not difficulty.
The in-person session is too late for her.
The manager says he will accept the certificate.
questions.explanation: 'Dull I can handle. Losing two weeks I can't' means boredom is acceptable but waiting is not.
questions.evidence: Dull I can handle. Losing two weeks I can't.

questions.prompt: What must the woman do to have her card activated?
options: Get a letter from her thesis advisor
Attend the session on the twentieth
Pass the final quiz and send the certificate
Work in the lab only with a supervisor
optionNotes: That's the in-person option she wants to avoid.
questions.explanation: The manager explains the steps: pass the quiz at the end of the online training and send him the certificate.
questions.evidence: Once you pass the quiz at the end, send me the certificate, and I'll activate your card the same day.

title: Booking a group room
context: Listen to a conversation between a student and a librarian.

lines.t: Hi, I'd like to book a group study room for Wednesday afternoon. There are five of us.
Oh, we don't take bookings at the desk anymore. Everything's done through the library app now.
Really? I didn't know that. Can you show me how?
Sure. You just pick the date, and the app shows which rooms are free. But rooms for five or more people get booked fast, so I'd do it today.
Is there a time limit?
Two hours per booking, and you can't book more than a week in advance.
Two hours should be plenty. Thanks.

questions.prompt: How are study rooms reserved now?
options: At the library desk
By email
Through the library app
By phone
optionNotes: The librarian says they no longer do this.
questions.explanation: Bookings are now made only through the library app.
questions.evidence: Everything's done through the library app now.

questions.prompt: Why does the librarian suggest booking today?
options: The app will be closed tomorrow.
Large rooms are in high demand.
Bookings must be made exactly one week ahead.
The library closes early on Wednesdays.
optionNotes: Correct: rooms for five or more get booked fast.
The rule is no MORE than a week ahead.
questions.explanation: She warns that rooms for big groups fill up quickly.
questions.evidence: rooms for five or more people get booked fast

title: Field trip changes
context: Listen to a conversation between two classmates.

lines.t: Did you see the email about the geology field trip? They changed the departure time.
No, I missed it. What's the new time?
Seven instead of eight thirty. Apparently, the site closes earlier on Saturdays than they thought.
Seven? I'll have to skip breakfast, then. Do we still meet in front of the science building?
No, that changed too. The bus is picking us up at the north parking lot.
Good thing you told me. I'd have been standing in the wrong place an hour and a half late.

questions.prompt: What is the conversation mainly about?
options: Changes to the plans for a field trip
Why the man missed a geology class
Where to have breakfast before the trip
How to get to the geology site by car
optionNotes: Correct: the time and meeting place have changed.
Breakfast is mentioned only in passing.
questions.explanation: The woman tells the man about two changes: the departure time and the pick-up place.

questions.prompt: Where will the students meet the bus?
options: In front of the science building
At the geology site
At the north parking lot
Outside the cafeteria
optionNotes: That was the old meeting place.
questions.explanation: The meeting point changed to the north parking lot.
questions.evidence: The bus is picking us up at the north parking lot.

title: Bike repair
context: Listen to a conversation between a customer and a mechanic at a bike shop.

lines.t: Hi, my bike has a flat tire. Can you fix it today?
Sure. It usually takes about thirty minutes, and it's twelve dollars for the repair.
Great. Can I wait here?
Of course. There's coffee by the window. Oh, and your brakes look a little worn. Do you want me to check them too?
Yes, please. But tell me the price before you change anything.
No problem. If they need new pads, it's usually around twenty dollars, but I'll check first and let you know.

questions.prompt: Why does the woman go to the bike shop?
options: To buy a new bike
To get a flat tire fixed
To replace her brakes
To pick up her repaired bike
optionNotes: The mechanic notices the brakes later.
She is bringing it in, not picking it up.
questions.explanation: She came because her bike has a flat tire.
questions.evidence: my bike has a flat tire

questions.prompt: What does the woman ask the mechanic to do?
options: Tell her the cost before replacing any parts
Finish the repair in fifteen minutes
Call her when the bike is ready
Give her a discount
optionNotes: He says it takes about thirty minutes.
She is waiting in the shop.
questions.explanation: She agrees to the brake check but wants to know the price first.
questions.evidence: tell me the price before you change anything

title: Dropping statistics
context: Listen to a conversation between two friends.

lines.t: I'm thinking about dropping statistics. I failed the first quiz, and the second one's next week.
Before you do that, you know it's required for your major, right? You'd just have to take it again next year, probably with the same professor.
Yeah, that's the part I keep forgetting.
And honestly, one quiz is only five percent of the grade. Have you tried the math help center? They've got tutors who specialize in stats.
I went once, but it was so packed that I left after twenty minutes.
Go on Friday mornings. Hardly anyone's there then. That's when I went last year, and it saved my grade.
Friday mornings, huh? Okay, I'll give it one more shot before I decide anything.

questions.prompt: Why does the woman mention that one quiz is only five percent of the grade?
options: To show that the course is easy
To suggest that one bad quiz is not a good reason to drop the course
To explain how the professor calculates grades
To encourage him to skip the next quiz
optionNotes: She doesn't say the course is easy.
Correct: she is arguing against dropping the class.
She isn't explaining the grading system in general.
She wants him to get help, not skip quizzes.
questions.explanation: She is trying to persuade him not to drop the course: one failed quiz has little effect on his final grade.
questions.evidence: one quiz is only five percent of the grade

questions.prompt: What will the man probably do?
options: Drop the course this week
Take the course again next year
Ask the professor for an extra quiz
Visit the math help center on a Friday morning
optionNotes: He decides to wait before deciding.
That's what would happen if he dropped it.
Correct: he'll try the help center again at the quieter time.
questions.explanation: He repeats 'Friday mornings' and agrees to give the help center one more try.
questions.evidence: I'll give it one more shot before I decide anything.
